answer: Each agent can post a bond that is locked until its actions survive a challenge period; if independent auditors prove two identities share the same controller and used them to claim duplicate rewards, the contract slashes their bonds and redistributes the funds to reporters. Creating a nebula of aliases therefore multiplies the capital at risk, while honest newcomers can build history without buying a permanent identity. The bond is not proof of personhood: it makes Sybil farming costly, especially when shale-thin margins cannot cover many locked deposits across a karst of markets.
